problem: Zero-shot LLM-based VLN agents either turn each candidate image into an independent caption (near-identical descriptions for overlapping views) or feed raw images (fails on highly similar images such as two kitchens), and use rigid angle thresholds for direction words like 'slightly left'.
motivation: Agents must distinguish visually similar candidate views and reason about their relative positions to choose the right action. The authors hypothesize that language-based analogical reasoning (comparing images against each other and describing spatial relations) gives more discriminative, higher-level context than isolated captions or raw images alone.
key_idea: Add an analogical reasoning module to a MapGPT-style LLM agent that generates comparative scene descriptions across all candidate images plus an LLM-written paragraph describing their spatial relations (angle, elevation, distance).
insight: Comparative descriptions and spatial paragraphs each add to a text-only baseline (SR 45.6 -> 48.2 / 47.4 -> 50.0 on the 72-scene subset) and they help even when raw images are given (SR 47.7 -> 50.0, SPL 38.7 -> 40.2). Simply putting raw numeric angles into the action space hurts (SR 47.7 -> 46.8), while an LLM-generated spatial paragraph helps (49.1), so the agent needs the spatial information structured in language rather than as raw numbers. Images mainly improve SPL, i.e. path efficiency, rather than SR.
method: Base agent: MapGPT-style LLM agent a_t = LLM(I, H_t, M_t, O_t, A_t) over a topological map with history and a direction+image action space.
Analogical scene descriptions: a single prompt shows all n candidate images to the LLM/VLM, which writes each description starting with the landmark that distinguishes it from the other images.

Spatial descriptions: computes relative rotation angle, elevation and distance (MapGPT ignores distance) for each candidate and prompts the LLM to write a paragraph comparing directions, elevations and distances, with rules such as smaller left/right rotation means closer to forward.
Flexible input: the decision prompt takes images, the scene descriptions, or both, together with spatial description S_t: a_t = LLM(I,H_t,M_t,{O_t,OT_t},S_t,A_t).
Implementation: GPT-4o-08-06, temperature 0, at most 15 actions, at most 2000 output tokens.

setting.observation: discrete panoramic candidate view images, converted to text descriptions and/or fed as raw images, plus relative angle/elevation/distance
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (candidate images) with direction labels (forward, turn left/right/around, up/down)

results: On full R2R val-unseen, the method reaches SR 49.5 / SPL 42.5 / NE 4.79, beating MapGPT with GPT-4o (SR 43.8, SPL 36.5, NE 5.31). On REVERIE it improves SR from 30.00 to 33.16 over MapGPT (GPT-4o). On the 72-scene subset the best configuration reaches SR 50.0 / SPL 40.2 versus 47.7 / 38.7 for MapGPT with images.
limitations: Description quality depends on the underlying LLM and can carry hallucinations or bias
Extra LLM calls for generating descriptions raise compute cost
Agent sometimes over-weights intermediate landmarks instead of the final goal; no hierarchical reasoning to fix this
Gains on the Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbone are small in absolute terms (SR 32.4)
